frame_retriever then returns candidate chart frames at 382.0s, 385.0s, and 388.0s; these are alternative chart states, not an ordered proof by themselves.

Among those, chart_analyzer on frame_385.00.png (timestamp 385.0s) reports the fullest readable chart, titled "Most indebted countries (as of 2021)," with values Japan 200, Greece 200, Sudan 180, Eritrea 170, Singapore 160, Italy 150, and the remaining countries below 150. Excluding Japan leaves 4 countries above 150%, so the correct option is E.

planner_output.refinement_instructions: Build the trace from scratch. First state that the relevant evidence must come from the country debt-to-GDP comparison graphic, not from the general debt narrative. Use step 1 only to anchor the chart interval; do not assume the highest-confidence segment is chronologically special beyond being a candidate. In step 2, inspect the returned frame timestamps and treat them as alternative candidate chart states; do not assume retrieval order implies quality. In step 3, use the frame-level chart analysis result that actually shows the complete chart with readable country labels and values. The rewritten trace should explicitly list the countries whose debt-to-GDP ratios exceed 150%, then exclude Japan and count the remainder. If chart_analyzer gives an approximate set or indicates partial visibility in one frame, prefer the frame result with the fullest chart coverage and preserve any uncertainty rather than guessing. Update the final answer to the option matching the verified count.
